recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Any future change to server timezone discovery should be handled as a new substantive work-group decision rather than reviving the invalid HTTP Date-header mechanism.
issue_request: FHIR-7026 was Published/Persuasive with Modification and objected that clients could not know the server timezone assumed for date searches; the resolution requested an implementation note about the server communicating its timezone.
initial_application: The issue was initially applied in git-svn commit 4dba5ab8ce, which added source/http.html text saying servers should return the default timezone for date searches in HTTP response headers using the Date header.
additional_context: FHIR-17630 later added client-timezone guidance and client-side timezone recommendations. FHIR-42971 later determined that the HTTP Date-header timezone text violated HTTP semantics and resolved to remove it, replacing it with server default timezone discovery via the timezone extension on CapabilityStatement.meta. Both related issues already have reconciliation commits on the combined branch.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current source/capabilitystatement/capabilitystatement-notes.xml documents server default timezone discovery through CapabilityStatement.meta, source/http.html documents client-timezone header behavior, and source/search.html retains date-search timezone guidance. Restoring the old Date-header note would contradict the later applied FHIR-42971 decision.

related_jiras.note: Later published timezone-search guidance added the client-timezone header and client-side timezone recommendations that frame the current search behavior. Already represented on the combined branch.
Later applied decision removed the FHIR-7026 HTTP Date-header text and replaced it with CapabilityStatement.meta timezone-extension discovery. Already represented on the combined branch.
